html:
SMTO-EXE-0139 — The Mac hasn't given SMTO permission to control apps

GUID: f2e75678-4da7-51d9-89bb-0efab863d850
Slug: ui-accessibility-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The Mac running the Gateway hasn't allowed it to use Accessibility, which SMTO needs to read and press buttons in other apps. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Mac running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that Mac), open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility and switch on the Gateway's entry. macOS blocks any program from reading or pressing buttons in other apps until it is allowed here.
  2. Once no tasks are using that Gateway, restart it, or ask whoever manages that Mac to restart it. The Gateway reports the new permission to SMTO when it starts and reconnects.
  3. In SMTO, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a new task. Tasks that were already running keep the abilities they started with; a new task picks up the new permission.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows that Gateway as connected, and a new task can read and press the app's buttons.

If it still fails

  • If the Gateway already looks allowed, switch its Accessibility entry off and on again, then check once more. If it still fails, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Mac. Don't use other tools to get around the Mac's privacy settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • macOS UI readiness found AXIsProcessTrusted false, so the Gateway reported Accessibility permission denied and did not advertise semantic UI actions.

What this means

  • macOS readiness found AXIsProcessTrusted false and reported accessibility permission denied before advertising semantic UI actions. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • macOS readiness found AXIsProcessTrusted false and reported accessibility permission denied before advertising semantic UI actions.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Accessibility permission for the actual Gateway host executable and its interactive session.

How to fix it

  • On the macOS Gateway host, enable the Gateway's host executable in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Then refresh the Gateway's capabilities (restart or reconnect an outbound Gateway; Check connection in Settings › Setup › Gateways re-reads them for a direct Gateway) and start a new task. Semantic AX does not need Screen Recording or Input Monitoring; ui.status should then report accessibility_permission granted.
  • On macOS enable the Gateway host in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, then refresh Gateway metadata. No Screen Recording or Input Monitoring permission is needed for semantic AX.

Retry and execution caution

  • On macOS enable the Gateway host in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility, then refresh Gateway metadata. No Screen Recording or Input Monitoring permission is needed for semantic AX.

How to verify the fix

  • ui.status reports granted Accessibility access for that executable and semantic UI readiness.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
